we have developed a facile approach to fabricate highly efficient thermoelectric (ZT ~10−3) nanocomposite foamed materials using non-conductive polymer foams and hybrid carbon nanostructures.

we developed an industrially viable technique to fabricate organic thermoelectric materials with enhanced energy generation efficiency using non-conduct polymer foam substrates and hybrid carbon nanofillers.

the use of macroporous polymer foams as substrates for the fabrication of TE nanocomposites with segregated 1D and/or 2D carbon nanofillers can significantly improve TE properties of organic TE nanocomposites.

the design and development of novel polymer-based nanocomposite foaming technology.
a new class of thermoelectric materials that are based on a polymer matrix and contain 1D and/or 2D nanofillers (e.g., CNTs and graphene nanoplatelets).
the development of a facile processing strategy for fabricating thermoelectric ( TE) polymer nanocomposites with non-conductors.

the present study provides a facile processing strategy to develop organic TE materials with non-conductors using hybrid 1D and/or 2D nanofillers, which can be potentially scaled up to fabricate flexible, lightweight and low-cost TE foams for energy conversion applications.

the proposed strategy to fabricate macroporous PVDC nanocomposite foils with 2D and 1D carbon nanomaterials represents a promising strategy to fabricate organic thermoelectric materials with improved energy conversion efficiency.
the present study demonstrates the potential of fabricating light-weight, low cost and flexible TE materials with high ZT values.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current study demonstrates a facile and industrially viable approach for developing organic thermoelectric (OTE) materials.
we developed a new approach for making thermoelectric materials with non-conductors.
we have developed an effective approach to fabricate TE polymer nanocomposite foam with non-conductors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of 1D and/or 2D nanofillers with open-cell polymer foams can be used to fabricate organic thermoelectric materials.
the combination of macroporous substrates, non-conducting polymer matrix, and hybrid nanofillers can be a promising strategy to develop high performance TE nanocomposites.
the combination of 1D and/or 2D nanofillers in the LBL assembly of TE nanocomposites can be used to fabricate TE nanocomposites with high electrical conductivity.
